identity: SCRIPTURE - Quran, Surat al-Baqara 261-273, the passage on spending in the way of God (the grain with seven ears, the smooth rock, the garden on a hill, Satan promising poverty, the poor who do not beg). Uthmani spelling with the diacritics and verse markers stripped (أمولهم، سنابل، الءاخر، الثمرت، الءايت، الشيطن، الألبب، بسيمهم), 310 tokens, ZERO <NL>.
law: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k), now the fourth scripture document and the second Quranic one. 310 tokens / 13 ayat = 23.8 tokens per verse - much longer than the 14.4 of Surat al-Nahl, which is a useful correction: verse LENGTH varies by sura, so the arithmetic check must be done against the identified passage, not against a corpus average. Inside a verse NOTHING cuts.
reasoning: The passage is thirteen long verses and every one of them contains material that my PASS-2 rules would cut. Suppressed: the vocative-plus-imperative openings of 2:264 and 2:267 (ya ayyuha alladhina amanu la tubtilu / anfiqu - E6 is dead in scripture, 0k); the fa-chains of the two parables (fa-asabahu wabil fa-tarakahu saldan in 2:264, and fa-asabaha isar fihi nar fa-htaraqat in 2:266, where four fa-clauses and a wa-clause all sit in ONE verse); wa-lakinna in 2:272; the conditional pairs of 2:271; and above all the closing formula wa-llahu X Y, which appears seven times (wasi alim, ghani halim, la yahdi al-qawm al-kafirin, bima tamalun basir, ghani hamid, wasi alim, bima tamalun khabir) and is always the LAST phrase of its verse, never the start of a new one. That formula is in fact the best alignment check available here: seven of the thirteen verse ends are marked by it. The two remaining risks were the twin openings alladhina yunfiquna amwalahum fi sabil allah at 2:261 and 2:262 - the second begins a new verse with no connective at all, so the boundary at @23 rests on the formula, not on syntax - and 2:273, which opens with a bare li-l-fuqara that reads like a continuation of 2:272 and is nonetheless its own verse. The last verse end lands exactly on the final token of the document.
